description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Discrete Mathematics topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: discrete-maths

facts.claim: An equivalence relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive

source.quote: an equivalence relation is a binary relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive

facts.claim: ≥ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric (a partial order idea)

source.quote: The relation "≥" between real numbers is reflexive and transitive, but not symmetric

facts.claim: Bijective = injective and surjective

source.quote: A function is bijective if and only if it is both injective (or one-to-one)

facts.claim: A bijection has an inverse

source.quote: the inverse of f, such that each of the two ways for composing the two functions produces an identity function

facts.claim: Countable = finite or in one-to-one correspondence with ℕ

source.quote: can be put in one to one correspondence with the set of natural numbers

facts.claim: The real numbers are uncountable (Cantor)

source.quote: who proved the existence of uncountable sets

facts.claim: Base case proves the first value

source.quote: The first, the base case, proves the statement for

facts.claim: Inductive step: if true for n then true for n + 1

source.quote: prove that for every n, if the statement holds for n, then it holds for n + 1

facts.claim: Euclid's algorithm computes the GCD

source.quote: the Euclidean algorithm, or Euclid's algorithm, is an efficient method for computing the greatest common divisor (GCD)

facts.claim: Replace the larger number by the remainder

source.quote: replacing the larger of the two numbers by its remainder when divided by the smaller of the two

facts.claim: Every integer > 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way

source.quote: every integer greater than 1 is either prime or can be represented uniquely as a prod

facts.claim: n distinct objects have n! permutations

source.quote: The number of permutations of n distinct objects is n factorial

facts.claim: A permutation is an ordering (arrangement)

source.quote: It can be interpreted as a new order of the members of a sequence

facts.claim: n items in m < n containers → some container has two or more

source.quote: if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item

facts.claim: Propositions are true or false

source.quote: It deals with propositions (which can be true or false)

facts.claim: Connectives: conjunction, disjunction, implication, biconditional, negation

source.quote: logical connectives representing the truth functions of conjunction, disjunction, implication, biconditional, and negation

facts.claim: Proof by contradiction: assume the opposite and reach a contradiction

source.quote: In mathematics, the technique is called proof by contradiction

facts.claim: Assume P is false and show that leads to falsehood

source.quote: We assume P to be false

facts.claim: A group: associative, identity, inverses (plus closure)

source.quote: the operation is associative, it has an identity element, and every element of the set has an inverse element

facts.claim: Integers under addition: identity 0

source.quote: Zero is called the identity element of addition

facts.claim: An Eulerian trail uses every edge exactly once

source.quote: visits every edge exactly once

facts.claim: Euler cycle iff every vertex has even degree (connected graph)

source.quote: A connected graph has an Euler cycle if and only if every vertex has an even number of incident edges

facts.claim: No two adjacent vertices share a colour

source.quote: no two adjacent vertices are of the same color

facts.claim: The chromatic number is the fewest colours needed

source.quote: the chromatic number problem
